title: Boss: read a trace like on-call
summary: A trace export from a failed checkout and a list of headers seen at each hop: find the span that caused the failure, the span that cost the time, and the hop that broke the trace.

steps.title: The ticket
body: **OPS-4410: "checkout returns 502 sometimes, and some traces stop at the shop".** You have Jaeger's export of one failing trace
(this one, recorded in the lab), and from the mesh's access logs the `traceparent` each service received for another request.
The spans come to your code as `record SpanRec(string Id, string? Parent, string Service, string Name, string Kind, double Start, double Dur, string Status, int? HttpStatus);`

attrs.db.query.text: UPDATE stock SET qty = qty - $1 WHERE product_id = $2 AND qty >= $1
attrs.db.system.name: postgresql

logs.body: Reservation failed for sku 12: stock conflict in warehouse eu-2 (code INV-5821)

steps.title: The root cause span
prompt: Errors propagate up: the server span is red because the checkout span is red because a client call is red. The interesting one is
- the root cause is the error span (`Status == "error"`) with **no error span among its descendants**;
- if there are several, take the one that **started first**;
- describe it as `"{Service} {Name} ({Kind})"`, plus `" -> {HttpStatus}"` when it has one, plus, when one of its **children** is a
- with no error span return `"no error"`.
solution: bool ErrorBelow(SpanRec s) => spans.Where(c => c.Parent == s.Id).Any(c => c.Status == "error" || ErrorBelow(c));
var callee = spans.FirstOrDefault(c => c.Parent == cause.Id && c.Kind == "server");
if (callee is not null) text += $" answered by {callee.Service} {callee.Name}";
hints: A recursive local function `bool ErrorBelow(SpanRec s)` that looks at the children and their children.
In the recorded trace the answer is the second `POST` client span (409); inventory's server span for it is Unset, as the HTTP conventions say for a 4xx.
template: Dojo.Eq("the recorded failed checkout", "shop POST (client) -> 409 answered by inventory POST /reservations", RootCause(dojoErr));
Dojo.Eq("no errors", "no error", RootCause(dojoErr.Select(s => s with { Status = "unset" }).ToList()));
Dojo.Eq("two leaf errors: the earlier one", "api GET (client) -> 503", RootCause(dojoDb));
record SpanRec(string Id, string? Parent, string Service, string Name, string Kind, double Start, double Dur, string Status, int? HttpStatus);

steps.title: Where did the time go?
prompt: Write `List<string> TopSelfTime(List<SpanRec> spans, int n)`: the `n` spans with the most **self time** (duration minus the time
covered by its direct children; children may overlap each other, so merge their intervals first, and clip them to the parent),
largest first, ties by `Start`, each as `"{Service} {Name} {self:F1}ms"`.
Overlap matters: a parent of 100 ms with two children running **in parallel** from 0 to 60 ms has 40 ms of self time, not -20.
solution: .Select(c => (From: Math.Max(c.Start, s.Start), To: Math.Min(c.Start + c.Dur, end)))
if (from >= reach) { covered += to - from; reach = to; }
else if (to > reach) { covered += to - reach; reach = to; }
return spans.Select(s => (s, Self: Self(s))).OrderByDescending(x => x.Self).ThenBy(x => x.s.Start)
hints: Turn each child into an interval clipped to the parent, sort by start, and sweep: add only the part beyond what is already covered.
template: Dojo.Eq("the slow product page: one query", new List<string> { "shop postgresql 92.5ms", "inventory postgresql 0.4ms" }, TopSelfTime(dojoSlow, 2));
Dojo.Eq("parallel children overlap", new List<string> { "api GET orders 60.0ms", "api GET profile 50.0ms", "api GET /dashboard 40.0ms" }, TopSelfTime(dojoPar, 3));
var dojoLate = new List<SpanRec> { new("p", null, "api", "job", "internal", 0, 10, "unset", null), new("c", "p", "api", "async tail", "internal", 5, 20, "unset", null) };
Dojo.Eq("a child that outlives its parent is clipped", new List<string> { "api async tail 20.0ms", "api job 5.0ms" }, TopSelfTime(dojoLate, 5));
record SpanRec(string Id, string? Parent, string Service, string Name, string Kind, double Start, double Dur, string Status, int? HttpStatus);

steps.title: Which hop broke the trace?
prompt: For a second request, the access logs give, in call order, the `traceparent` each hop **received** (null when there was none):
`record Hop(string Service, string? Received, string SentSpanId);` where `SentSpanId` is the span id the hop put in the header it sent on.
Write `string BrokenHop(List<Hop> hops)`. The first hop is the edge and starts the trace (its `Received` is ignored). For every later hop,
the received header must be valid (paste in your `TryParse`), carry the **same trace id** as the previous valid header, and name the
previous hop's `SentSpanId` as its parent. Return the first hop that fails as
`"{Service}: no traceparent"`, `"{Service}: invalid traceparent"`, `"{Service}: new trace id"` or `"{Service}: wrong parent"`,
solution: if (h.Received is null) return $"{h.Service}: no traceparent";
if (!TryParse(h.Received, out var t, out var parent, out _)) return $"{h.Service}: invalid traceparent";
if (trace is not null && t != trace) return $"{h.Service}: new trace id";
bool TryParse(string? header, out string traceId, out string parentId, out bool sampled)
static bool Hex(string s, int len) => s.Length == len && s.All(c => c is >= '0' and <= '9' or >= 'a' and <= 'f');
if (parts[1].All(c => c == '0') || parts[2].All(c => c == '0')) return false;
hints: Walk from the second hop; remember the trace id of the first valid header you saw.
Order of checks: missing, invalid, a different trace id, then the parent id against `hops[i - 1].SentSpanId`.
template: Dojo.Eq("a worker that never got a header", "inventory: no traceparent", BrokenHop([dojoGood[0], dojoGood[1], dojoGood[2] with { Received = null }]));
Dojo.Eq("a proxy that upper-cased it", "shop: invalid traceparent", BrokenHop([dojoGood[0], dojoGood[1] with { Received = $"00-{dojoT.ToUpperInvariant()}-1111111111111111-01" }, dojoGood[2]]));

Dojo.Eq("a service that started its own trace", "inventory: new trace id", BrokenHop([dojoGood[0], dojoGood[1], dojoGood[2] with { Received = "00-0af7651916cd43dd8448eb211c80319c-2222222222222222-01" }]));
Dojo.Eq("a header forwarded unchanged (the old parent)", "inventory: wrong parent", BrokenHop([dojoGood[0], dojoGood[1], dojoGood[2] with { Received = $"00-{dojoT}-1111111111111111-01" }]));
record Hop(string Service, string? Received, string SentSpanId);
